extracted_text: Archaeological Survey of Western India 1876. Volume II: Memoranda on the Antiquities of Kathiawad and Kachh by James Burgess, F.R.G.S., Archaeological Surveyor and Reporter to Government.

Survey of Anahilavada Pattana (Modern Patan). The subterranean stepped well known locally as the Rani ki Vav, or the Queen's Stepwell, situated to the northwest of the city, was commissioned by Queen Udayamati, the consort of Bhimadeva I (c. 1022–1064 CE). Merutunga in his Prabandha-Chintamani expressly states that Udayamati, daughter of Naravahana Khengara of Saurashtra, caused this vast stepped excavation to be constructed, surpassing even the Sahasralinga tank in devotional splendour.

Architectural Arrangement and Galleries: The monument measures approximately 65 metres in length and 20 metres across, descending into the aquifer across seven distinct terraces or storeys of pillared galleries (kutas). The columns exhibit typical Solanki (Maru-Gurjara) bracket capitals and carved shafts. The western retaining wall forms a cylindrical well shaft 30 metres deep, revetted with finely dressed sandstone masonry.

Sculptural Program: Over five hundred principal figurative sculptures adorn the subterranean galleries. Dominant is the Vaishnava iconography: the Dashavatara including the boar incarnation (Varaha) lifting Bhudevi, Vamana, Narasimha disemboweling Hiranyakashipu, Rama, and Balarama. At the lower levels closest to the water table, reclines Sheshashayi Vishnu upon the serpent Ananta, symbolizing the cosmic waters at the dawn of creation.

Modhera Sun Temple Comparison: Notes on the contemporaneous Surya temple at Modhera on the banks of the Pushpavati river, constructed under Bhimadeva I in 1026 CE. The Sabha Mandapa (Assembly Hall) and Surya Kund stepwell reveal identical masonry coursing, stepped corbelled ceilings, and torana ornamental arches characteristic of 11th century Chaulukya artisans.

Svasti. Om Namah Shivaya. Royal charter of the Chaulukya kings of Anahillapataka. In the lineage of Mularaja, King Bhimadeva ruled with righteousness, subduing the Malwa armies and restoring the sacred shrines of Somanatha. His chief queen, the pious Udayamati, endowed perpetual grants for scholars, ascetics, and travelers visiting the sacred stepped waterworks.

Translation and Epigraphical Notes: The inscription confirms the genealogical succession: Mularaja -> Chamundaraja -> Durlabharaja -> Bhimadeva I (Chaulukya). Explicit mention of water management architecture (vapi / dirghika) as the supreme charitable merit (purta-dharma) under the Chaulukya kings of Gujarat.

extracted_text: Architectural Survey of the Sun Temple at Modhera (1886). The grand temple dedicated to Surya stands on the river Pushpavati. Built in 1026 CE during the reign of King Bhima I of the Chaulukya dynasty, the complex comprises the Gudhamandapa (shrine hall), the Sabhamandapa (assembly hall), and the magnificent stepped water tank known as Surya Kund.

The Surya Kund: A rectangular stepped tank measuring 176 feet by 120 feet, adorned with 108 miniature shrines arranged symmetrically along the terraced stepped descent to the water. Intricate carvings depict Ganesha, Sheshashayi Vishnu, and various forms of Shiva Nataraja.
